At 0% research progress, prioritize a small, reproducible extension of the supplied HSTU diagnostic adapter. No measured results currently establish which intervention improves validation HR@10.

**Insights from the starting point.** First, qualitative feedback favors specific recent purposes over broad historical associations. This motivates measuring dependence on recent interactions, without assuming that dependence proves intent. Second, single-negative margins describe local separation. They cannot establish whether the target survives top-10 competition. Third, left padding makes readout correctness essential. Diagnostics must select the final nonpadding position and use the actual trained HSTU through ModelView.

**Insights from related work.** HSTU identifies positional/temporal attention and multiplicative gating as architectural components [1]. Their presence in the supplied implementation must be verified before proposing component ablations. Sequence-pattern research separates behavioral order from catalog availability [2]. Consequently, shuffled-history effects require cautious interpretation. Sampled-metric research shows that candidate sampling can change model comparisons [3]. The pinned benchmark must remain the selection criterion, with diagnostic rankings reported separately.

The framework has three directions:

| Direction | Existing evidence | Proposed extension | Interpretation limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Recent-history dependence | Qualitative feedback; sequence research | Paired history perturbations | Dependence does not identify intent |
| Ranking competition | Positive–negative margins | Fixed 99-negative target ranks | Diagnostic samples differ from benchmark |
| Evidence sufficiency | Metadata; selective prediction [4] | Explicit unknown states | Missing specifications imply uncertainty |

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of 10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Paired recent-history rank probe — 4/8/3.** Originality: + combines HSTU-compatible interventions with competitive ranks; − established perturbation methods. Potential: + localizes useful follow-up experiments; − does not itself improve ranking. Difficulty: + reuses inference hooks; − requires careful masking and paired sampling [1–3].
2. **Representation-spectrum probe — 2/6/2.** Originality: + adds history-feature analysis; − effective rank is established. Potential: + distinguishes shared direction from dimensional concentration; − low rank need not indicate ranking failure. Difficulty: + bounded SVD; − centering and normalization affect interpretation [5].
3. **Metadata evidence ledger — 4/6/5.** Originality: + separates unknown compatibility from explicit conflict; − adapts selective prediction. Potential: + grounds qualitative diagnosis; − specifications may be absent. Difficulty: + deterministic extraction is feasible; − reliable conflict rules require domain-specific parsing [4].

Select **idea 1**, given its low implementation cost and direct connection to the feedback. For fixed training users, reserve each history’s final training item as a diagnostic target; these remain in-sample measurements. Compare intact history, recent-suffix-only history, and equal-count removal of recent versus older interactions. Reuse identical candidates across conditions.

```text
sample users and unique unseen negatives with seed 42
for each user and history condition:
    left-pad; obtain final nonpadding HSTU feature
    score target and identical 99 negatives
report paired rank changes, hits, and top-10 overlap
bootstrap paired user outcomes within category
macro-average category means
```

Preserve both diagnostic entry points, return explicit metric definitions and sample counts, and mark insufficient samples unavailable. Keep one unchanged trained checkpoint per category. Use host validation HR@10 for subsequent model selection; diagnostic effects alone justify no performance claim.

idea.description: Extend the family-aware diagnostic adapter with paired recent-history perturbations and fixed-candidate target ranks, inspecting each category’s single trained HSTU.
idea.motivation: The feedback suggests that broad historical associations may outweigh specific recent purposes, while existing single-negative margins do not measure top-10 competition. Paired interventions can reveal model dependence and guide subsequent training hypotheses without asserting causal intent.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Use view.model in evaluation mode under torch.no_grad(), restoring its previous training state afterward. Build deterministic bounded diagnostic cases from view.user_train['History']; hold out the last training interaction only for diagnostic scoring, explicitly labeling results in-sample because model training may already have included it. Draw 99 unique real-item negatives excluding the target and the user's training history; report insufficient-catalog cases as unavailable. Set removal count k=min(5,floor((history_length-1)/2)) and require k>=1, ensuring both removal conditions retain nonempty histories. Preserve surviving item order, left padding, and any implemented timestamp alignment. Read features at the greatest index containing a nonzero item, never count-1. Score candidates through predict_score without assuming dot-product scoring. Define target rank using a documented deterministic item-ID tie break; define hit as rank<=10. Compute top-10 overlap on the same 100-item diagnostic set and label its scope. Bootstrap paired users within each category and equally average category means; report group sizes and unavailable metrics explicitly. Do not infer compatibility, fulfilled needs, or simulator traits from these effects. Do not access unavailable metadata fields or test files. Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, all four routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, and the host evaluator unchanged. This diagnostic-only proposal leaves the architecture, checkpoint format, and embedded predictor unchanged; later architecture changes must update the predictor writer consistently.
idea.pseudocode:
run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    existing = measure_existing_probes(train_loader)
    cases = fixed_training_history_cases(view.user_train, seed=42, bounded=True)
    save model mode; set eval
    for case in cases:
        target = case.last_training_item
        history = case.preceding_training_items
        candidates = [target] + sample_99_unique_unseen_items(seed=42, user=case.user)
        if insufficient history or candidates: record unavailable; continue
        k = min(5, (len(history)-1)//2)
        variants = {intact: history, suffix: history[-min(10,len(history)):], remove_recent: history[:-k], remove_old: history[k:]}
        for name, surviving_history in variants:
            sequence = left_pad_and_truncate(surviving_history)
            features = view.log2feats(sequence)
            final_index = max(nonzero_indices(sequence))
            scores = view.predict_score(features[:, final_index], candidates)
            record rank, hit_at_10, candidate_top_10
        record paired differences and overlap with intact condition
    restore model mode
    aggregate with paired user bootstrap within categories
    return {metrics: merge(existing, aggregates), metric_definitions: explicit_definitions}

diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    embed measured metrics, definitions, sample counts, and unavailable states
    require conclusions to distinguish model dependence from user intent
    identify all training-prefix measurements as in-sample

originality.positive: Combines competitive target ranks and matched history interventions within the supplied HSTU diagnostic contract.
originality.negative: Perturbation analysis and paired ranking comparisons are established techniques.

future_potential.positive: Can guide focused experiments on recent-history weighting and reveal category-specific failure patterns.
future_potential.negative: Diagnostic sensitivity does not establish causal intent or guarantee improved validation HR@10.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses the trained model and existing inference interfaces without additional fitted predictors.
code_difficulty.negative: Requires careful candidate exclusion, left-padding readout, timestamp alignment where supported, and paired aggregation.

related_work.title: [1] Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations
contributions: Introduces HSTU and describes positional/temporal attention bias and multiplicative gating.
limitations: Does not establish diagnostic thresholds or the benefit of the proposed perturbations on these four Amazon datasets.

related_work.title: [2] Disentangling User and Item Sequence Patterns
contributions: Examines sequence effects with shuffling controls that account for item availability.
limitations: Ordinary history perturbations can mix behavioral order effects with catalog effects; sensitivity alone cannot identify intent.

related_work.title: [3] On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can change comparisons relative to full-catalog evaluation.
limitations: Does not replace the task's mandated pinned sampled-candidate selection metric.

related_work.title: [4] Sufficient Context
contributions: Studies context sufficiency alongside confidence for selective answering.
limitations: Its question-answering findings motivate a proposed diagnostic adaptation, not an established recommendation improvement.

related_work.title: [5] The Effective Rank: A Measure of Effective Dimensionality
contributions: Defines effective rank using the entropy of normalized singular values.
limitations: Representation dimensionality alone does not establish recommendation quality or embedding collapse.
